title: Check similarity between two texts
description:
Write a function `text_similarity(path1, path2, stop_words)` that reads the two text files, removes every word in `stop_words` from each (case-insensitive), and returns their Jaccard similarity: the number of words the two texts have in common, divided by the number of distinct words across both, rounded to 4 decimals.

Compares real transcripts - Michelle Obama's and Melina Trump's speeches, both available in your working directory.

hints: Idea to consider: turn each text into a set of words (after removing stop words), then compare the sets

For two sets, `len(a & b) / len(a | b)` is their Jaccard similarity - identical sets score 1.0, completely disjoint sets score 0.0, and it naturally lands somewhere in between for two real speeches that share ordinary vocabulary but differ in subject.
Read and tokenize both files, drop any word in stop_words from each (case-insensitive), turn the results into sets, and return the intersection-over-union ratio, rounded to 4 decimals.
expected_behavior: Returns the Jaccard similarity of the two texts' vocabularies, stop words excluded, rounded to 4 decimals.
explanation: Stop words are removed before comparing because otherwise two texts in the same language would look artificially similar just from sharing 'the', 'and', 'is' - the interesting overlap is in the topic-specific vocabulary that's left after common function words are stripped out.
